newsitem.title: USA: Most NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, AGAs seen neutral.
newsitem.headline: Most NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, AGAs seen neutral.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, pressured by light profit taking, mostly ended lower Wednesday in sluggish trade, then drifted sideways on ACCESS after weekly AGA stock data fell within expectations, sources said.
March slipped 6.7 cents to close at $2.43 per million British thermal units. April settled 4.5 cents lower at $2.224. Others ended mixed, with some 1999s up slightly.

"It (AGA) was in line. I think anything over 150 (bcf) was fairly positive, but utilities are still coming out of storage and not coming out of the pipe, and there's no real weather driving us," said one Midwest trader.

AGA said U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 161 bcf, in line with expectations, with overall stocks about 45 bcf above year-ago. But the report showed eastern stocks grew to 158 bcf, or 23 percent, above last year's levels.

With just six more weeks of winter left and inventories in the critical consuming region east at a hefty surplus to 1996, traders said only a sustained bout of Arctic cold could rally prices significantly from here.
Most expected increasing pressure on storage operators and utilities to trim stock levels, particularly in the East, to limit any upside in the cash.

Technical traders said long liquidation pressured the complex today. They pegged March resistance in the low-$2.50s and then in the $2.70 and $2.80 area. Trendline support was seen in the low-$2.30s and then at the November 5 low of $2.12.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed more than five cents Wednesday to the low-$2.60s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the $2.50 area. New York city gate swing gas held relatively steady in the low-$3 level.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell two cents to $2.22. NYMEX said an estimated 26,921 Hub contracts traded, down from Tuesday's revised tally of 30,631.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Wednesday.

On the KCBT, March finished six cents lower at $2.14, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.7 cent to 29 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 164 contracts traded, up slightly from Tuesday's total of 157.
